No propositions came through, so I can't pick among them. The strongest general refutation I know is that the calculus needs pleasures and pains to sit on one cardinal scale that is comparable across persons, and no such scale exists. The team note's claim that pain and pleasure are inevitable features of life doesn't refute anything, because Bentham's theory already assumes that. Paste the options and I'll say which one matches.
